Notes on the closer calls: `f_1fa8e96c3cfd` (operator: Google) is the textbook "operator inferable from the name" case — Chrome/Lighthouse implies Google, but the span never says it. `f_e01b7fb2cd0f` vs `f_df82f9e3ceb4` share the same span ("This is usually RSS or Atom") but diverge in the fact's claim: "aliases: RSS" mischaracterizes a format example as a naming relation (fabrication), while "The feed is usually RSS or Atom" is a faithful paraphrase modulo the pronoun "This" resolving to "feed" via the window (subject_dropped). `f_92b0e8e9c6e3` is the weakest fit to the taxonomy — the span defines patterned fields as the implementation of extension properties, but "extend the specification" as the object comes from the window's preceding sentence, not the span itself; I mapped it to `subject_dropped` as the closest available class but flag lower confidence there.
